questions.question_raw: [image-based question: picture of a tick, looked like Dermacentor]

parts.text: Name one infection associated with this tick.

parts_raw.text: Name 1 infection associated with this tick.

questions.model_answer: a) Rocky Mountain spotted fever (Rickettsia rickettsii). Dermacentor spp. (D. variabilis, the American dog tick, and D. andersoni, the Rocky Mountain wood tick) are the principal vectors; other acceptable Dermacentor-associated infections include tularemia, Colorado tick fever, and tick paralysis.

questions.question: Ixodes scapularis (eastern black-legged tick) is a vector for multiple pathogens.

parts.text: Name one virus, one parasite, and two bacteria that are transmitted by this vector.

parts_raw.text: Ixodes scapularis. Name one virus, one parasite, 2 bacteria that are transmitted by this vector.

questions.model_answer: a) Virus: Powassan virus (deer tick virus lineage), a Flaviviridae/tick-borne encephalitis virus. Parasite: Babesia microti (babesiosis), an intraerythrocytic protozoan. Bacteria: (1) Borrelia burgdorferi (Lyme borreliosis) and (2) Anaplasma phagocytophilum (human granulocytic anaplasmosis). [Other acceptable bacteria: Borrelia miyamotoi (relapsing-fever-like borreliosis) and Ehrlichia muris eauclairensis.]
